domain_restrictions: M, A, B, A_prime, and B_prime are polynomials with integer coefficients
E, F, and G are rational functions with rational coefficients
gcd of B and M is 1
gcd of B_prime and M is 1
The congruence relation is defined only through the existence of such a representation of the difference F minus G
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: If a rational function E equals F minus G and E can be expressed as M times a polynomial numerator divided by a polynomial denominator that is coprime to M, then F and G are congruent modulo M in the stated sense, because their difference has such a representation.
quantifier_order: For every nonzero polynomial M in Z[q]
for every rational functions E, F, and G in Q(q)
assuming E equals F minus G
assuming there exist polynomials A and B in Z[q] such that gcd of B and M is 1 and E equals M times A divided by B
then F is congruent to G modulo M, meaning there exist polynomials A_prime and B_prime in Z[q] such that gcd of B_prime and M is 1 and F minus G equals M times A_prime divided by B_prime

witness_dependencies: The assumed witnesses A and B depend on the pair M and E, not directly on F and G except through the identity E equals F minus G
The conclusion witnesses A_prime and B_prime can be taken to depend on the same earlier witnesses A and B; in fact the same A and B already witness the conclusion because F minus G equals E
No additional hidden witness beyond A, B, A_prime, and B_prime is required

statement_nl: Let M(q) be a nonzero polynomial in Z[q], and let E(q), F(q), and G(q) be rational functions in Q(q). Assume that E(q) = F(q) - G(q). Assume also that there exist polynomials A(q) and B(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B(q), M(q)) = 1 and E(q) = M(q) A(q) / B(q). Then F(q) ≡ G(q) mod M(q), where by definition F(q) ≡ G(q) mod M(q) means that F(q)-G(q) can be written as M(q) A'(q) / B'(q) for some polynomials A'(q), B'(q) in Z[q] with gcd(B'(q), M(q)) = 1.
